name: hauling-gate
description: Arrival-gated debris hauling (issue #437): 'vehicle haul <id> fragment:<id>' sets hauling intent only — a debris_hauler then drives to the blast fragment, loads it only on arrival, drives to the nearest freight_warehouse, and delivers it only on arrival. Immediately after the haul command (before the first post-command tick block), the fragment must still be on_ground/untransported — the state dump right after 'vehicle haul' proves the task did not start/complete instantly. After the first tick 20 the vehicle should be in transit (fragment picked up, hauling toward the depot) or already delivered; after the following tick 40 the fragment must be state:stored and logistics.storedMassKg increased.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 4 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(25,25) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

expect.note: the driver already holds driving.truck at level 1 from ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION -- this call is a same-level no-op

steps.description: The Haul button always picks the vehicle's nearest reachable, non-oversized, storage-fitting fragment (findReachableGroundFragment, HaulEligibility.ts) -- not a fixed index. #785 is what that function itself returns for this exact seed/command sequence (confirmed by calling it directly), which is why this id looks arbitrary rather than a round number picked by hand -- it must be re-derived the same way if anything upstream (the grid, the blast, the vehicle's spawn point) ever changes. Re-derived from #531 during the depth-mismatch audit (Ground rule #15/Finding #42): correcting this file's drill_plan depth from 8 to 6 (the grid tool's real default, since this step never clicks the depth stepper) changes the whole blast/fragment population, invalidating the old hardcoded id -- confirmed the hard way, the first pass at the depth fix left #531 in place and storedMassKg silently stayed 0 through both tick 20 and tick 40 (fragment #531 no longer exists in the corrected population), exactly the kind of regression a fixed-id hack risks and the file's own note above already warned about.

expect.note: sets hauling intent only -- the fragment is not yet loaded, proving 'vehicle haul' does not complete instantly (#437)

steps.description: Confirmed via direct trace (seed:42) that the full pickup-drive-deliver cycle completes within this window -- storedMassKg is already at its final value by the end of this step, not just 'in transit'.

expect.note: storedMassKg is deliberately not asserted to an exact value here: findReachableGroundFragment (the real Haul button's own fragment choice) is sensitive to the vehicle's exact tick-by-tick position, and interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (Finding #12) can in principle pick a different -- but equally valid -- fragment than command mode's clean tick10. Historically (before the depth-mismatch audit's fragment-id re-derivation above) the delivered amount genuinely differed between modes (263.25kg in command mode vs 1050kg in a real browser run); since the fragment is now pinned explicitly by id (`vehicle haul 1 fragment:785`) rather than left to each mode's own opportunistic re-targeting, both modes now deliver the identical 1050kg -- confirmed directly, both modes re-run after the fix. Left as increased/undereasserted-exact rather than hard-pinning 1050kg here too, since this step's own point is proving delivery completed at all (tick 20's increased:[storedMassKg] already does that), not re-asserting the amount a second time.
